subject: weird segfault problem with rstan (only with parallel sampling, only on one computer)

messages.author: ebac19664dad3407
messages.subject: weird segfault problem with rstan (only with parallel sampling, only on one computer)
parts:
I have a weird segfault problem with rstan. I see it with both version 2.6.0 and 2.7.0-1.

I have two machines running Debian 8.1 (jessie), both up to date via apt-get update, upgrade, and dist-upgrade, and both up to date with R 3.2.1 and update.packages()

One machine is a workstation and the other is a laptop (a Lenovo Thinkpad W541). I see segfaulting only on the laptop and never on the workstation.

rstan runs the 8schools model fine on both machines, running 10,000 iterations both with serial sampling and with parallel sampling (mclapply for rstan 2.6.0 and with setting cores > 1 on rstan 2.7.0-1).

However, I am working on a large multilevel mixture model. This model runs correctly when I sample the chains serially. But when I sample the chains in parallel it runs fine on the workstation whereas on the laptop it consistently (every time) segfaults on some (but not all) of the chains.  The segfaults don't happen right away. They typically run for tens to hundreds of iterations before one or more chains segfaults with "address (nil), cause 'unknown' " (always that exact message).

I do the stan run from the command line using Rscript and I monitor the run with htop, which shows that I always have at least 20 GB of RAM free. I also have plenty of free space on all my disk partitions, so it's not an issue of running out of room for temporary files.

After a chain segfaults, the R script continues to run and the other chains continue to sample.

I'm attaching my model and a driver script, the sessionInfo() output, the stderr output for the crash (but I edited down the printout of the function call arguments on lines 9 and 10 of the traceback, which printed out a data list with more than 20,000 elements)

The laptop is very new and I've seen some weirdness at boot time with the Linux drivers not quite being up to date for the chipset and sometimes failing to initialize the machine properly, so my problem might be an OS driver issue, not a stan issue. On the other hand, I have not had segfaulting problems with other software on this laptop after a successful boot, except for rstan when I'm doing parallel sampling. Also, I ran stress-ng for about 8 hours and didn't get any errors.

So I'm not at all sure that this is a stan issue but it might be, so I'm reporting it just in case other people see something similar.

I do almost all my nontrivial stan computing on my workstation, not my laptop, so the fact that a few large models are segfaulting on the laptop when I sample in parallel is not preventing me from getting my work done. Thus, unless other people are having similar problems, this is probably a low priority issue with respect to the stan team's valuable time and energy.

If there is other useful information that I can provide, I'd be happy to do that.
